ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a nitrogen-containing heterocycle fused with a benzene ring. The upper carbon of the heterocycle on the right is connected to a neutral hydroxyl O-H and also bears R2; the lower-right carbon is connected to R1; the lower nitrogen in the ring is labeled as positively charged N-H. The curved arrows in the figure indicate that electrons move along the ring within the heterocycle, while the left benzene ring part remains unchanged. Reasoning: After moving the π electrons from the arrow tails to heads, keep O as neutral OH and keep nitrogen as protonated [N+]([H]). The new bond orders appear as the nitrogen forming an iminium-type double bond with the fused carbon, while a C([*])=C bond forms between the carbon bearing R1 and the carbon bearing OH/R2. Using [*] to represent R1 and R2, the product SMILES obtained is OC1([*])C2C=CC=CC2=[N+]([H])C([*])=C1.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a benzene-fused N-containing ring with OH/R2 at the upper carbon, R1 at the lower-right carbon, and [N+]H in the ring. Label the key ring atoms, then follow each curved arrow tail-to-head to shift the pi bonds around the heterocycle. Keep the benzene ring unchanged, retain O as neutral OH, and keep nitrogen protonated and positively charged. The relocated-electron state has the iminium-like N+ double bond to the fused carbon and a C([*])=C bond to the OH/R2-bearing carbon. Encode that product graph with R1 and R2 as [*] to obtain OC1([*])C2C=CC=CC2=[N+]([H])C([*])=C1.
